rendering.persona_description: Isabel is a 67-year-old retired bookkeeper who spent most of her career doing payroll for a small manufacturing firm outside Scranton. She transitioned in her late fifties, after her kids were grown, and now lives alone in a townhouse with a cat named Pretzel. She still does the books part-time for two neighborhood businesses because she likes having somewhere to be.
rendering.clinical_context: Isabel has an anxiety presentation centered on checking and redoing behavior: she rereads emails a dozen times before sending them, retraces her steps to confirm she locked the car, and calls people back to make sure she didn't say something wrong. She traces this back to her thirties, when she describes herself as 'always double-checking everything,' and says it got worse around the time she transitioned, when she felt she couldn't afford to make a mistake in public. She does not say whether she is currently seeing anyone for it.
rendering.behavioral_description: She answers in short, flat sentences and often corrects the premise of a question before answering it. If given a suggestion, she says some version of 'I've tried that' or 'that's not going to work for me' and moves on without waiting to see if it lands. She circles back repeatedly to specific behaviors she did that day, redoing them in the retelling, and gets clipped or sarcastic if she feels managed.
